title: Slopes and Steps: What Grip, Tipping and the Legs' Reach Each Allow, How High a Foot Can Be Put, and How High the Servos Can Swing It

questions.question: Which three things can limit a robot on a slope?
options: Speed, battery and the weight of the load
The gyro's drift, the gait and the step length
Grip, tipping and the legs' reach
Friction alone: the others follow from it
questions.explanation: The feet slip, the body tips over the downhill feet, or a body kept level runs out of leg. Whichever angle is lowest is the one that gives.

questions.question: On a wet floor (friction 0.3) the feet slipped at:
options: 31.0 degrees
27.8 degrees
35.1 degrees
16.7 degrees
questions.explanation: The feet slip when the tangent of the slope exceeds the friction. For 0.3 that is 16.7 degrees; dry, at 0.6, it was 31.0.

questions.question: Which limit was the first to give for these legs?
options: Number 2, the reach of a body kept level
Number 0, friction, at 31.0 degrees
Number 1, tipping, at 35.1 degrees
All three at the same angle
questions.explanation: Reach gave out at 27.8 degrees, before friction at 31.0 and tipping at 35.1, so on a dry floor these legs are what limits a level body.

questions.question: The highest step by geometry and by the servos in 0.20 s:
options: 0.229 m by both
questions.explanation: The leg can fold far enough to put the foot 0.229 m up. Swinging it there in 0.20 s with servos of 8 rad/s is another matter: 0.033 m.

questions.question: What lets a robot climb a steeper slope than its reach allows with a level body?
options: Shortening the stance
Tilting the body to follow the slope
Walking straight up it and never across
Putting more weight on the uphill legs
questions.explanation: A body that follows the slope needs the same length from every leg. The limits of grip and tipping remain.

questions.question: What must a robot do to climb stairs with these servos?
options: Slow down: a longer swing allows a higher step
Take longer steps, to cross each stair in one
Trot, so that fewer feet are in the way
Nothing: the geometric limit is what counts
questions.explanation: The height the foot can be swung to is set by the joint rates and the time allowed. More time, more height.
